turns.question: How do errors propagate through the middleware composition path?
turns.agentText:
<ghx-report>
{
  "answer": "Errors propagate via two nested try/catch layers plus a settable handler. Inside compose()'s dispatch(i) (src/compose.ts), each middleware call is wrapped in try/catch: if the thrown value is `instanceof Error` and an `onError` callback was supplied, it calls `onError(err, context)` (sets `context.error`, marks `isError=true` so the response is force-assigned to `context.res` even if not finalized); otherwise it rethrows up the async chain. Hono's `#dispatch` (src/hono-base.ts) passes `this.errorHandler` as that `onError`, and also wraps the `composed(c)` await in its own try/catch calling `#handleError`, which re-invokes `this.errorHandler` for Error instances or rethrows non-Error throws (making them fatal/unhandled); the same `#handleError` also guards the single-handler fast path that bypasses compose() entirely. `this.errorHandler` defaults to the module-level `errorHandler` (returns `err.getResponse()` for HTTPException-like errors, else logs and returns a generic 500) and can be overridden via `app.onError(handler)` at hono-base.ts:271.", 
  "verified": [
